sentences.en: So, you know, Vance gives this speech at the Munich Security Conference.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，万斯在慕尼黑安全会议上发表了这篇演讲。

sentences.en: It's like this massive event, probably the most high profile security forum globally, where you have tons of heads of state, prime ministers, defense ministers,
sentences.zh: 这就像是一场规模宏大的活动，可能是全球最受瞩目的安全论坛，台下坐着成群的国家元首、首相、国防部长、

sentences.en: foreign ministers in the audience.
sentences.zh: 外交部长。

sentences.en: We're happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: And, you know, one of the things that I wanted to talk about today is, of course, our shared values.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我今天想谈的事情之一，当然是我们共同的价值观。

sentences.en: But instead of talking about Trump's foreign policy, he launches into this extensive criticism of Europe.
sentences.zh: 但他没有谈论特朗普的外交政策，而是对欧洲展开了广泛的批评。

sentences.en: The threat that I worry the most about vis-a-vis Europe is not Russia, it's not China, it's not any other external actor.
sentences.zh: 我最担心的关于欧洲的威胁不是俄罗斯，不是中国，也不是任何其他外部行为者。

sentences.en: And what I worry about is the threat from within, the retreat of Europe from some of its most fundamental values, values shared with the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 而我担心的是来自内部的威胁，欧洲对其最根本价值观的退缩，这些价值观与美利坚合众国所共有。

sentences.en: You know, a Europe that, in his telling, has departed from its democratic roots.
sentences.zh: 你知道，按照他的说法，一个已经偏离其民主根基的欧洲。

sentences.en: It's actually a picture of Europe that very much echoes what we've been hearing from Vladimir Putin over the last few years.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一幅在很大程度上呼应了我们过去几年从弗拉基米尔·普京那里听到的话的欧洲画卷。

sentences.en: You know, he's long been criticizing Europe for becoming too woke, for silencing speech.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他长期以来一直批评欧洲变得过于“觉醒”（woke），压制言论。

sentences.en: And I really do believe that allowing our citizens to speak their mind will make them stronger still.
sentences.zh: 我真的坚信，允许我们的公民表达他们的心声将使他们更加强大。

sentences.en: Which, of course, brings us back to Munich,
sentences.zh: 当然，这又把我们带回了慕尼黑，

sentences.en: where the organizers of this very conference have banned lawmakers representing populist parties on both the left and the right from participating in these conversations.
sentences.zh: 在这里，这次会议的组织者禁止代表左翼和右翼民粹主义政党的议员参与这些对话。

sentences.en: Now again...
sentences.zh: 现在再说一次……

sentences.en: And, you know, and even more remarkable was the fact that he was doing this in Germany with the big national German election less than two weeks away.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，甚至更引人注目的是，他在德国这样做时，距离德国的大规模国民大选还不到两周。

sentences.en: And where the German far-right party is hoping to make big gains.
sentences.zh: 而德国极右翼政党正希望借此取得重大斩获。

sentences.en: And, of course, the German far-right party, the alternative for Germany,
sentences.zh: 当然，德国极右翼政党——德国选择党，

sentences.en: has been very much ostracized across the political spectrum in Germany for its links to neo-Nazi ideology and its attempts to whitewash the Nazi paSt.
sentences.zh: 因其与新纳粹意识形态的联系以及试图美化纳粹历史的行径，在德国整个政治光谱中一直遭到强烈排挤。

sentences.en: If you're running in fear of your own voters, there is nothing America can do for you.
sentences.zh: 如果你连自己的选民都害怕，那美国也帮不了你。

sentences.en: Nor for that matter is there...
sentences.zh: 话又说回来，也没有……

sentences.en: Basically, the vice president of the United States is saying to his European allies, long-standing European allies, that Russia isn't the problem here, you are.
sentences.zh: 基本上，美国副总统是在对他的欧洲盟友——长期以来的欧洲盟友说，俄罗斯不是这里的问题所在，你们才是。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And Vance here is signaling the possibility that America will no longer be that key ally of Western Europe and the European Union that it was for all those decades after the end of World War II.
sentences.zh: 万斯在这里释放出一个信号：美国可能不再扮演二战结束数十年来它对西欧和欧盟所扮演的那种关键盟友角色。

sentences.en: We shouldn't be afraid of our people even when they express views that disagree with their leadership.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该害怕我们的人民，即使他们表达的观点与领导层不一致。

sentences.en: Thank you all.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: Good luck to all of you.
sentences.zh: 祝你们好运。

sentences.en: God bless you.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑你们。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: But that the Europeans probably won't be there.
sentences.zh: 但欧洲人大概不会在场。

sentences.en: And it's worth pointing out that it would be pretty striking for Europe to be excluded like this.
sentences.zh: 值得指出的是，欧洲被这样排除在外将是非常令人震惊的。

sentences.en: You know, European countries have contributed more than $100 billion, by some counts, more than the U.S.
sentences.zh: 要知道，据某些统计，欧洲各国在过去三年里向乌克兰提供的资金超过了1000亿美元，甚至超过了美国援助的总和。

sentences.en: has in total, to Ukraine over the last three years.
sentences.zh: 所以他们显然在这件事上也拥有巨大的利害关系。

sentences.en: So they clearly have a huge stake in this too.
sentences.zh: 所以他们显然在这件事上也拥有巨大的利害关系。

sentences.en: Okay, basically, it sounds like Europe's out, but Ukraine is in.
sentences.zh: 好吧，基本上听起来像是把欧洲排除在外了，但乌克兰还在局中。

sentences.en: Well, maybe.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许吧。

sentences.en: I mean, there's so much uncertainty right now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在有太多的不确定性。

sentences.en: In fact, we're actually continuing to see signs that Ukraine's involvement is in question.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们仍在不断看到乌克兰的参与受到质疑的迹象。

sentences.en: Just this weekend, we learned that three top U.S.
sentences.zh: 就在这个周末，我们得知三位美国高级官员——

sentences.en: officials, Marco Rubio, the Secretary of State, Mike Waltz, the National Security Advisor, Steve Witkoff, the Middle East envoy,
sentences.zh: 国务卿马可·卢比奥、国家安全顾问迈克·沃尔兹、中东特使史蒂夫·维特科夫，

sentences.en: are all going to be in Saudi Arabia to meet with Russian officials about the war in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 都将前往沙特阿拉伯，与俄罗斯官员会面讨论乌克兰战争。

sentences.en: And for all we know, Ukraine won't be there.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，乌克兰将不会出席。

sentences.en: So in that sense, it's not a surprise that when Volodymyr Zelensky was on Meet the Press on Sunday morning, he was insisting that Ukraine did need to be involved.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基周日早上在《会见新闻界》节目中坚持认为乌克兰必须参与其中，也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: Okay, but just to ask a really basic question, how do you end a war in Ukraine without Ukraine at the table?
sentences.zh: 好的，但问一个非常基础的问题，如果没有乌克兰坐在谈判桌前，怎么能结束乌克兰战争呢？

sentences.en: Well, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是个好问题。

sentences.en: It is true, Rachel, that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 雷切尔，美国确实是乌克兰最大的盟友。

sentences.en: is Ukraine's biggest ally.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基自己也说过，如果美国撤回援助，乌克兰很难作为独立国家存活下去。

sentences.en: And Zelensky himself has said that if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基自己也说过，如果美国撤回援助，乌克兰很难作为独立国家存活下去。

sentences.en: were to pull its aid, it would be very difficult for Ukraine to survive as an independent country.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基自己也说过，如果美国撤回援助，乌克兰很难作为独立国家存活下去。

sentences.en: On the flip side, Putin has also made it very clear that he wants to be talking to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，普京也明确表示他希望与美国对话。

sentences.en: You know, he sees Zelensky's government as a puppet of Washington.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在他看来，泽连斯基政府不过是华盛顿的傀儡。

sentences.en: So there is clearly space here for conversations between the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，美国和俄罗斯之间显然有进行对话的空间。

sentences.en: and Russia to happen.
sentences.zh: 美俄之间进行对话本无可厚非。

sentences.en: It would just be pretty shocking for those conversations to happen without Ukraine being a part of them.
sentences.zh: 只是如果这些对话将乌克兰排除在外，那就太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: But the second issue is that even if Russia and the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但第二个问题是，即便俄罗斯和美国在这里达成协议，你知道，你仍然需要乌克兰对此表示同意。

sentences.en: were to make a deal here, you know, you would still need Ukraine to agree to it.
sentences.zh: 你需要乌克兰同意停止战斗。

sentences.en: You would need Ukraine to agree to stop fighting.
sentences.zh: 而泽连斯基已经非常明确地表示，乌克兰绝不接受他们未曾参与谈判的协议。

sentences.en: And Zelensky has said very clearly that Ukraine will not accept a deal that they were not a part of in negotiating.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果这些谈判变得更加严肃，最大的问题将是如何在普京的要求与乌克兰的需求之间找到平衡点？

sentences.en: So the big question, if these negotiations get more serious, is going to be how do you thread the needle between Putin's demands and what Ukraine would need?
sentences.zh: 你知道，普京不仅要求保留他已经占领的领土，还希望对乌克兰施加影响力。

sentences.en: You know, Putin is demanding not just to keep the territory he already has, but he also wants influence over Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 他希望限制乌克兰的军事力量。

sentences.en: He wants Ukraine's military to be limited.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，泽连斯基和乌克兰人则表示，他们需要安全保障。

sentences.en: And then on the other hand, Zelensky and the Ukrainians are saying they need security guarantees.
sentences.zh: 他们需要确凿的保证，即如果普京将来再次试图入侵，将会遭到回应。

sentences.en: They need assurances that there will be a response if Putin were to try to invade again down the road.
sentences.zh: 他们需要对俄罗斯形成威慑。

sentences.en: They need deterrence against Russia.
sentences.zh: 他们需要对俄罗斯形成威慑。

sentences.en: And so how to thread the needle between those two things, that's clearly going to be really hard.
sentences.zh: 因此，如何在这两者之间寻找平衡，显然会非常困难。

sentences.en: And that's what we'll be watching from here.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们接下来将持续关注的焦点。

sentences.en: So obviously we know what Zelensky thinks Ukraine wants and what Ukraine needs, but I'm curious about average Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 显然我们知道泽连斯基认为乌克兰想要什么和需要什么，但我很好奇普通乌克兰人的想法。

sentences.en: Do we know how they feel about the war and peace talks and all of this?
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们对战争、和平谈判以及这一切的感受吗？

sentences.en: Well, we know from our colleagues in Ukraine that there's extremely deep skepticism across Ukraine that Putin can be seen as a good faith negotiator.
sentences.zh: 嗯，据我们在乌克兰的同事透露，整个乌克兰对普京能否成为一个诚心诚意的谈判对手抱有极其深刻的怀疑。

sentences.en: At the same time, you know, if you look at our colleagues reporting from Ukraine, you see there's intense fatigue with the war there.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，如果你看看我们同事从乌克兰发回的报道，你会发现那里对战争有着极度疲惫的情绪。

sentences.en: The war has lasted almost three years now, which would have been just so unimaginable if we think back to the beginning of 2022.
sentences.zh: 这场战争已经持续了将近三年，如果回想2022年初，这简直是难以想象的。

sentences.en: Obviously, tens of thousands of Ukrainians, both soldiers and civilians, have died.
sentences.zh: 显然，数以万计的乌克兰人，包括士兵和平民，已经失去了生命。

sentences.en: And so what you've also been seeing over the last year or so in Ukraine is a higher readiness, according to the polls, to make some kind of compromise with Russia.
sentences.zh: 因此，根据民调显示，在过去一年左右的时间里，乌克兰对与俄罗斯做出某种妥协的接受度也在不断提高。

sentences.en: Anton, I feel like it's worth taking a step back here and just reckoning with what a head-spinning week this has been.
sentences.zh: 安东，我觉得我们有必要退一步思考，意识到这是多么令人头晕目眩的一周。

sentences.en: We've basically seen the United States embrace Russia over its long-standing allies.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上看到美国抛弃了长期盟友，转而拥抱俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's still early, but you're right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，现在下定论还早，但你是对的。

sentences.en: It really feels like a moment where that world order that we were all used to has started to crumble.
sentences.zh: 这真的让人感觉，我们以往习惯的那个世界秩序已经开始崩塌了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Most people listening to this show have grown up in a world where it's a given that the United States is aligned with Europe.
sentences.zh: 大多数收听这个节目的人都在一个理所当然认为美国与欧洲结盟的世界中长大。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, there were clearly pretty major bumps along the way that we can remember.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，我们当然也经历过一些重大的波折。

sentences.en: But I struggle to remember a week like the one that we just saw, where J.D.
sentences.zh: 但我很难想起像刚过去这一周这样的情景——

sentences.en: Vance, Pete Hegseth, and Donald Trump himself just shook the foundations of that transatlantic alliance so intensely.
sentences.zh: J·D·万斯、皮特·海格塞斯以及唐纳德·特朗普本人，如此剧烈地动摇了跨大西洋联盟的根基。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you think back to Putin and the beginning of his invasion of Ukraine, in many ways, this is kind of what he wanted to achieve.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果你回想一下普京和他的乌克兰入侵之初，在很多方面，这正是他一直想要达到的目标。

sentences.en: You know, before Putin started his invasion, I don't know if you remember,
sentences.zh: 你知道，在普京发动入侵之前，我不知道你记不记得，

sentences.en: he presented this ultimatum to the West saying NATO needed to withdraw from Eastern and Central Europe and really give Russia its European sphere of influence back.
sentences.zh: 他向西方提出了最后通牒，称北约需要从东欧和中欧撤军，并真正把欧洲势力范围归还给俄罗斯。

sentences.en: At the time, that seemed like a ludicrous demand.
sentences.zh: 当时，这看起来像是一个荒谬的要求。

sentences.en: The West dismissed it out of hand.
sentences.zh: 西方当即予以拒绝。

sentences.en: But here we are three years later and really kind of talking about many of the things that Putin demanded.
sentences.zh: 但三年后的今天，我们居然真的在讨论许多普京当初提出的要求。

sentences.en: Look, make no mistake.
sentences.zh: 听着，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: The cost of all this to Russia has been just extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 这一切对俄罗斯而言代价极其高昂。

sentences.en: Maybe a hundred thousand or more Russians have died.
sentences.zh: 可能已经有十万或更多的俄罗斯人丧生。

sentences.en: Something like a million have fled the country.
sentences.zh: 大约有上百万人逃离了国家。

sentences.en: The economy has been stretched to its breaking point.
sentences.zh: 经济已经被逼到了崩溃的边缘。

sentences.en: Obviously, just the moral cost of having started Europe's biggest war of aggression since World War II is hard to fathom.
sentences.zh: 显然，发动自二战以来欧洲最大侵略战争所带来的道德代价更是难以估量。

sentences.en: But if Putin, through these peace talks, is able to settle the war more or less on his terms, that'll be something he presents as a big victory.
sentences.zh: 但如果普京通过这些和平谈判，或多或少按自己的条件解决这场战争，这将成为他的一大胜利。

sentences.en: And an even bigger victory will be if, at the end of all this, he gets the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而一个更大的胜利将是，这一切结束时，他成功让美国抛弃了欧洲。

sentences.en: to walk away from Europe.
sentences.zh: 而一个更大的胜利将是，这一切结束时，他成功让美国抛弃了欧洲。

sentences.en: Anton, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 安东，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，雷切尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Sunday, lawyers for President Trump asked the Supreme Court to let him fire the head of a federal agency that safeguards whistleblowers and enforces certain ethics laws.
sentences.zh: 周日，特朗普总统的律师要求最高法院允许他罢免一个联邦机构的负责人，该机构负责保护举报人并执行某些道德法律。

sentences.en: The move is the first test of the White House's broader challenge to limits on presidential authority and the ability of a president to fire the leaders of independent agencies that are meant to be insulated from politics.
sentences.zh: 此举是对白宫关于总统权力限制以及总统是否有权罢免本应独立于政治之外的独立机构领导人这一挑战的首次测试。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Alex Stern, and Mooj Zadie.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科、亚历克斯·斯特恩和穆杰·扎迪制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Maria Byrne and Patricia Willans.
sentences.zh: 由玛丽亚·伯恩和帕特里夏·威兰斯剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Dan Powell and Pat McCusker.
sentences.zh: 包含丹·鲍威尔和帕特·麦卡斯克的原创音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由来自Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Stephen Erlanger.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢斯蒂芬·埃兰格。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《切割机秀》中，我们正在为假期的节日待客做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种对光线极度敏感、需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会晕厥过去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在纽约时报应用上或你喜欢的任何地方搜索《切割机秀》。

sentences.en: Do they like to hear?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢听什么？

sentences.en: Be sure to come together.
sentences.zh: 务必聚在一起。

sentences.en: Do they can to sleep on the Wheeling digesters?
sentences.zh: 他们能在威灵消化器上睡觉吗？

sentences.en: For more sleepers, we have to hear something like that.
